rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of algorithmic rent-setting software that sets rents for residential rental property using nonpublic competitor data. Tenants need only prove the landlord used prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits; covers algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data such as real-time rents, lease renewals and occupancy levels.
rules.exemptions: Pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data or aggregate historical data, and tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the landlord uses software relying on nonpublic competitor data

rules.penalty: Affected tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rules.citation: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting ordinance (ordinance number and municipal code section not given in document)
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance, approved on Tuesday, Feb. 17, for a first reading and set for a final vote on March 3, prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
